chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May God keep you well! Has there been placed in the people a faculty by which they can attain recognition?' He said: So he (the Imam) said: 'No.'
I said: 'Then have they been charged with (attaining) recognition?' He said: 'No. Upon God is the clarification.'
God does not impose upon any soul a duty but to the extent of its ability [2:286], and God does not lay on any soul a burden except to the extent to which He has granted it [65:7].
He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about His words: 'It was not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them, until He clarifies to them what they should guard against [9:115].'
He said: 'Until He makes known to them what pleases Him and what angers Him.'

key_terms.أَدَاة: Ada (faculty/tool) — an innate cognitive or spiritual capacity; the question is whether humans possess such a natural faculty for recognizing God
key_terms.الْبَيَان: Al-bayan — the clarification, declaration; the divine responsibility to make known what is required before holding humanity accountable
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَة: Ma'rifa — recognition, gnosis, experiential knowledge of God; in Shia theology, specifically the recognition of God's oneness and the Imamate
key_terms.وُسْع: Wus' — capacity, ability; the extent of what one can bear or accomplish

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq teach that humans have an innate faculty for knowing God?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abd al-A'la questions Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether humans possess an innate faculty to achieve ma'rifa (recognition/gnosis of God). The Imam's response—that neither the tool nor the religious obligation exists by human faculty alone—reflects the Shia theological principle that divine guidance and clarification are prerequisites for religious accountability. The Imam supports this with two Quranic verses (2:286 and 65:7) establishing God's justice, and then interprets 9:115 as meaning that God first reveals what pleases and displeases Him before holding people accountable.
